turnaround_reason: Fourth-largest US IT staffing/solutions firm (formerly ASGN, rebranded Everforth in April 2026) de-rated on softening commercial demand and lengthening sales cycles; still solidly profitable and cheap at a cyclical trough.
bullish_points: Extraordinary coordinated insider cluster: five execs bought ~$2.18M open-market on Apr 24 2026 (CEO ~$1M at ~$19.24), day one after the blackout lifted — strongest insider signal in this batch
Genuinely profitable: net margin +2%, trailing P/E ~16 / forward P/E ~7.4, P/B 0.72, ~6-7x EBITDA, FCF $214M
Q2 beat (0.91 vs 0.82 est); Federal Government + data/AI segments provide ballast as commercial normalizes
Valuation near a historical trough with demand expected to normalize
bearish_points: Revenue -1.3%; commercial conversions slowing, enterprise software projects delayed (higher-margin mix pressured)
Debt/equity ~83; staffing is cyclical and structurally AI-exposed
Stock has already bounced ~90% off its 52-week low ($16.9 to ~$31.8), so some recovery is priced in
Analyst mean target $27.5 sits below the current ~$31.8 price
catalyst: Q3 earnings showing commercial stabilization / demand normalization
suggested_trade: Spot, medium starter position; the insider conviction is the standout. Jan 2027 calls if seeking leverage
key_risk: Commercial IT demand stays soft or AI structurally compresses staffing spend, capping the earnings recovery
would_skip_if: Q3 shows no commercial stabilization and sales cycles keep lengthening
